title: Open Wilson chain numerical renormalization group approach to steady-state non-equilibrium quantum transport
abstract: The numerical renormalization group (NRG) approach was developed to identify and quantify different equilibrium regimes of quantum impurity systems (QISs) with unprecedented accuracy by a tailored finite size representation. Out of equilibrium, the steady-state density operator is not of the Boltzmannian form but one that is determined by the imposed boundary conditions. We extend the NRG to the nonequilibrium setting by augmenting each Wilson site with a reservoir, whose coupling functions are calculated via a continuous fraction expansion in order to recover the continuum limit exactly. The nonequilibrium parameters such as a finite bias as well as a finite temperature gradient enters through the Bloch-Redfield tensor (BRT), whose zero eigenvector gives the steady-state density operator. We used the resulting open chain full density matrix (OC-FDM) approach with an effective single lead description to investigate the charge and spin transport through a quantum dot (QD) under finite bias and temperature gradient. The influence of lead asymmetry and an external magnetic field on the transport properties are also studied. For completeness, we have also investigated local properties of the QD, such as charge fluctuations and find excellent agreement with real-time quantum Monte Carlo (RT-QMC) data. The OC-FDM approach was able to explore Kondo energy scales as low as $T_K/D \approx 10^{-8}$ in the non-equilibrium regime, as well as show convergence with the established equilibrium benchmarks, such as a quantitative agreement with full density matrix numerical renormalization group (FDM-NRG) and Fermi-liquid scaling at small bias and temperature. Owing to the effective single lead description, a single OC-FDM data point takes orders of magnitude less time on a standard laptop, compared to other state-of-the-art numerical methods.
summary: The paper presents an extension of the Numerical Renormalization Group (NRG) technique, termed OC-FDM, to model non-equilibrium quantum transport in interacting junctions like quantum dots. By coupling the NRG structure to reservoir dynamics via the Bloch-Redfield tensor, it accurately calculates steady-state currents and spectral functions under finite bias or temperature gradients. This method offers a powerful, computationally fast tool for studying strongly correlated physics far from equilibrium.
main_problem: The study investigates non-equilibrium quantum transport through interacting junctions, specifically addressing how to accurately determine the steady-state density operator when driven by finite bias or temperature gradients.
main_result: The proposed Open Chain Full Density Matrix (OC-FDM) approach successfully extends NRG techniques to the non-equilibrium regime, achieving high accuracy for Kondo physics while being computationally efficient compared to other state-of-the-art methods.
method: The method combines the Numerical Renormalization Group (NRG) framework with the Bloch-Redfield master equation formalism. It constructs an effective single-lead description by solving the density matrix evolution iteratively across NRG shells.
model_or_system:
The system modeled is a Quantum Dot (QD) or quantum impurity coupled to two leads, described by a Hamiltonian involving Coulomb repulsion and coupling terms. The transport is analyzed under non-equilibrium conditions like finite bias ($\mu_L 
eq \mu_R$) or temperature gradients ($T_L 
eq T_R$).
key_observables: Charge and spin currents ($I_\alpha$), differential conductance ($dI/dV$), spectral functions $A(\omega)$, and the steady-state density operator $ho_{	ext{steady}}$.
important_parameters: Finite bias voltage ($eV$), temperature gradient ($\Delta T$), external magnetic field ($h_0$), and Kondo energy scales ($T_K$).
main_assumptions: The OC-FDM approach assumes that density matrix elements of discarded states remain unaltered across NRG iterations, which is necessary to solve the master equation in a manageable form.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spectral functions $A(\omega)$ and differential conductance ($dI/dV$) under varying bias and magnetic fields, demonstrating Kondo peak splitting and convergence with established benchmarks.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon NRG for equilibrium systems by augmenting Wilson sites with reservoirs. It introduces the OC-FDM approach to solve the steady-state density operator via the Bloch-Redfield Tensor (BRT) in the non-equilibrium setting, applying this to calculate transport properties like current and conductance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes advanced numerical techniques (NRG) into the complex domain of open quantum systems far from equilibrium. The ability to handle Kondo physics under bias/gradient using a computationally efficient method is valuable for modeling nanoscale devices.
